title: Israel asks Rehoboam to lighten the heavy yoke Solomon imposed
speaker: Jeroboam and the assembly of Israel
note: Request answered in 10:5; parallel 1 Kings 12:4 is also unrecorded and could be Additional Scripture.

title: Solomon’s elders counsel Rehoboam to win the people with kindness
speaker: the elders who had served Solomon
note: Counterpart of the young men’s counsel (ot-2-chronicles-v10-10); parallel 1 Kings 12:7 also unrecorded.

title: Israel renounces David’s house and calls its tribes home
speaker: the people of Israel
recipient: Israel’s tribes, with a taunt to David’s house
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Secession cry 'To your dwellings, Israel!'; parallel 1 Kings 12:16 also unrecorded. 10:15 is narrative.

title: Asa commands Judah to seek the Lord and keep the law
speaker: King Asa
note: Reported royal command; 14:2 is narrative of the reform.

title: Asa’s assembly covenants to seek the Lord on pain of death
speaker: King Asa and the assembly
recipient: Judah, Benjamin and the Israelites living among them
note: Covenant stipulation with death penalty (15:13), sworn with trumpets (15:14); AUD-14-15-1 covers only 15:1–7.

title: Jehoshaphat sends officials, Levites and priests to teach the law
speaker: King Jehoshaphat
recipient: his officials, the Levites and the priests
note: Adjacent gap, not a flagged candidate (17:5 itself is narrative); chapter 17 has no records.

title: Jehoshaphat asks Ahab to seek the Lord’s word before battle
speaker: King Jehoshaphat of Judah
note: Ordinary request; parallel 1 Kings 22:5 also unrecorded.

title: The messenger urges Micaiah to echo the prophets’ favorable word
speaker: the messenger sent to summon Micaiah
note: Pressure to conform the prophetic word, refused in 18:13; parallel 1 Kings 22:13 also unrecorded.

title: Micaiah recounts a spirit being permitted to deceive the king’s prophets
speaker: Micaiah, recounting the Lord’s word
note: The vision and the Lord’s call for a volunteer (18:18–20) open the same commission; extend to 18:18–21.

title: Ahab tells Jehoshaphat to wear his robes while he goes in disguise
speaker: Ahab king of Israel
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Chronicles parallel of 1 Kings 22:30. 18:27 'Hear, all you peoples' is a call to witness; no record.

title: Jehu rebukes Jehoshaphat for helping the wicked and loving the Lord’s enemies
speaker: Jehu son of Anani the prophet
note: Prophetic rebuke implying a prohibition on alliance with the wicked; rhetorical-question form, hence low.

title: Jahaziel tells Judah to go out and watch the Lord deliver them
speaker: Jahaziel, speaking the Lord’s word
note: 'Tomorrow go down against them', with the enemy’s position; same oracle and directive. Extend to 20:16–17.

title: Jehoiada assigns priests and Levites to Sabbath gate duty
speaker: Jehoiada the priest
note: Completes the assignment by thirds begun in 23:4 (cf. 2 Kings 11:5–6 records); extend to 23:4–5.

title: Jehoiada covenants that king and people be the Lord’s people
speaker: Jehoiada the priest
note: Covenant stipulation; 23:17 (Baal’s house destroyed) is its outworking. Parallel 2 Kings 11:17 also unrecorded.

title: The Lord’s prophets and Azarias son of Jehoiada call Judah back
speaker: the Lord through his prophets and Azarias son of Jehoiada
note: Prophets sent 'to turn them back' (24:19) and Azarias’s rebuke for transgressing the commandments; cf. ot-2-kings-v17-13.

title: Joash orders Azarias son of Jehoiada stoned in the temple court
speaker: King Joash
topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
note: Reported royal order in the context verse; 24:22 dying words are an appeal to God, out of scope.

title: Amaziah challenges Joash, who answers with the thornbush story
speaker: Joash king of Israel
note: Joash’s application of the fable, 'Now remain in your house'; extend to 25:17–19 (cf. 2 Kings 14:10).

title: Hezekiah orders the priests to offer sin offerings for all Israel
speaker: King Hezekiah
note: 29:21 order to go up to the altar; 29:24 royal ruling that the offerings are for all Israel.

title: Hezekiah orders the burnt offering begun with song and trumpets
speaker: King Hezekiah
note: Reported order; follows the instrument arrangements of AUD-14-29-25 (29:25–26), which could instead be extended.

title: Hezekiah tells the Levites to sing praise in David’s and Asaph’s words
speaker: King Hezekiah and the rulers
note: Reported call to worship using the words of David and Asaph the prophet.

title: Hezekiah’s assembly decrees a second-month Passover for all Israel
speaker: King Hezekiah, his rulers and the assembly in Jerusalem
recipient: all Israel, from Beersabee to Dan
note: Royal decree behind the Passover letters (30:6–9 records); compare the second-month Passover law C0841 (Numbers 9:10–11).

title: Hezekiah organizes the priestly and Levitical divisions and funds the offerings
speaker: King Hezekiah
note: 31:2 assigns divisions and duties; 31:3 sets the king’s portion for daily, Sabbath and festival burnt offerings.

title: Hezekiah commands Judah to worship and burn incense at one altar
speaker: King Hezekiah, as quoted by Sennacherib’s envoys
recipient: Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem
note: Quoted royal decree centralizing worship; parallels 2 Kings 18:22 and Isaiah 36:7 are also unrecorded.

title: Keep all the law given through Moses to remain in the land
speaker: the Lord, recalled by the narrator
note: Conditional covenant requirement recalled; parallel 2 Kings 21:7–8 unrecorded; compare ot-2-kings-v17-37.

title: Manasseh commands Judah to serve the Lord God of Israel
speaker: King Manasseh, after his repentance
note: Adjacent gap, not a flagged candidate; chapter 33 has no records. Same kind as Asa’s command (14:3).

title: Josiah sends his scribe to the high priest about the silver
speaker: King Josiah
note: Chronicles parallel of 2 Kings 22:3–4 (the sending is in context verse 34:8).

title: Josiah directs that the silver go to the temple repair workers
speaker: King Josiah, carried out by those appointed in the temple
note: Narrated execution of the 2 Kings 22:5–6 directive; 34:12 names the Levite overseers.

title: Huldah tells the officials to take the Lord’s answer back to Josiah
speaker: Huldah the prophetess, speaking the Lord’s word
note: Second 'this is what you shall say to him' charge in the same oracle; extend to 34:23–26 (cf. 2 Kings 22:18).

title: Josiah covenants to keep the Lord’s commandments and binds the people
speaker: King Josiah
note: Covenant to keep commandments with whole heart and soul; 34:33 adds enforced service. Parallel 2 Kings 23:3 also unrecorded.

title: Alexander divides his kingdom among his officers before his death
speaker: Alexander the Macedonian
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Authority handed on in narrative; include only if the catalogue keeps such historical transfers.

title: Antiochus appoints overseers and orders every Judean town to sacrifice
speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
recipient: his kingdom and the towns of Judah
note: Enforcement clause after the decree records for 1:41–50: overseers appointed and sacrifice ordered city by city.

title: Mattathias refuses the king’s decree and vows to keep the covenant
speaker: Mattathias
note: Declared refusal to obey the king against the law; compare A051 (Acts 5:29) and AUD-16-6-21 (Eleazar).

title: The fugitives resolve to defend themselves on the Sabbath
speaker: Mattathias and his friends
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: The deliberation that produces the 2:41 resolution; extend to 2:40–41.

title: Mattathias charges his sons to repay the nations and keep the law
speaker: Mattathias
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Same deathbed charge continues ('Repay the nations… attend to the law’s command'); extend to 2:67–68.

title: Victory comes from Heaven, not from the size of an army
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
note: Declarative saying in Judas’s speech; the following command not to fear is recorded separately (3:22).

title: Antiochus pays his army a year’s wages and orders it ready
speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
note: Reported royal order.

title: Antiochus leaves Lysias regent and orders him to destroy Judea
speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
note: Regency and guardianship of the heir (3:32–33) with orders to crush Judea and resettle its land (3:34–36).

title: Lysias sends Ptolemy, Nicanor and Gorgias to destroy Judah
speaker: Lysias
recipient: Ptolemy son of Dorymenes, Nicanor and Gorgias
note: Carries out the king’s command; parallel account 2 Maccabees 8:8–9 (also proposed under P01151).

title: Judas sends home the exempt according to the law
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
recipient: those building, betrothed, planting vineyards, and the fearful
note: Applies Deuteronomy 20:5–8 'according to the law', as 2 Chr 25:4 is linked to C1176; 3:55 echoes C1094.

title: Better to die in battle than to watch the nation’s ruin
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
note: 'Better… than' saying with submission to Heaven’s will after the 3:58 command; could instead extend ot-1-maccabees-v3-58.

title: Judas urges his army to fight today for their brothers
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
note: Battle exhortation at the relief of the besieged city (5:31–33).

title: Judas asks Ephron for peaceful passage through its land
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Request for passage in the context verse; Moses’s similar offer is only Study Context (ot-deuteronomy-v2-28), hence low.

title: Judas orders his company to encamp where they stand
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
note: Reported order by proclamation before the assault on Ephron.

title: Joseph and Azariah seek a name for themselves in battle
speaker: Joseph and Azariah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Their orders to march on Jamnia carry out the 5:57 resolve, against Judas’s command (5:19); extend to 5:57–58.

title: Dying Antiochus appoints Philip regent and guardian of his heir
speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Appointment with diadem, robe and ring to bring up the heir to reign (recalled at 6:55).

title: Lysias makes the young Antiochus king and names him Eupator
speaker: Lysias
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Royal appointment that sets aside Antiochus’s choice of Philip as guardian.

title: Judas assembles the people to besiege the citadel in Jerusalem
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
note: Reported summons without speech; record only if such musters are kept.

title: Renegade Israelites urge the king to act quickly against Judas
speaker: ungodly men from Israel who escaped the blockade
note: Petition for vengeance; also covers P01081 (6:27). Compare Alcimus’s similar petition (ot-1-maccabees-v7-7).

title: Antiochus Eupator breaks his oath and orders Zion’s wall torn down
speaker: King Antiochus Eupator
note: Reported order breaking the sworn peace of 6:60–61.

title: Demetrius sends Nicanor with orders to destroy the people
speaker: King Demetrius
note: Reported commission of a commander to destroy Israel.

title: Nicanor threatens to burn the temple unless Judas is handed over
speaker: Nicanor
recipient: the priests and elders on Mount Zion
note: Demand in the adjacent verse 7:35 (7:33 is narrative); compare 2 Maccabees 14:33.

title: The people establish the Day of Nicanor on the thirteenth of Adar
speaker: the people of Judah
note: 1 Maccabees account of the same annual festival decree recorded at 2 Maccabees 15:36.

title: Rome warns Demetrius to stop oppressing its Jewish allies
speaker: the Roman Senate
note: Warning letter reported after the treaty (AUD-15-8-24, 8:24–30); could instead extend that record.

title: Judas proposes fighting while his men urge retreat
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Judas’s reply, 'let us die courageously for our brothers', completes the exchange; extend to 9:8–10.

title: Bacchides appoints ungodly men as masters of the country
speaker: Bacchides
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Appointment by a hostile governor; 9:26 records its outworking.

title: Judas’s friends choose Jonathan to lead them in Judas’s place
speaker: all Judas’s friends
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: The people commission a leader (9:30), accepted in 9:31; compare AUD-07-11-8 (Jephthah).

title: Alcimus orders the wall of the inner temple court demolished
speaker: Alcimus
note: Reported order 'tearing down the works of the prophets'; 9:55 records his being struck.

title: Jonathan sends envoys to seek peace and the captives’ return
speaker: Jonathan
note: Reported request granted under oath (9:71–72); 9:70 sits in P01096’s context.

title: Demetrius authorizes Jonathan to raise an army and frees the hostages
speaker: King Demetrius, by letter
note: Grant of authority and order to hand over the hostages, read publicly in 10:7–9.

title: Jonathan orders Mount Zion’s walls rebuilt with four-foot stones
speaker: Jonathan
note: Reported order, with its execution.

title: Alexander appoints Jonathan high priest and the King’s Friend
speaker: King Alexander, by letter
note: Seleucid appointment to the high priesthood, taken up at the Festival of Booths (10:21).

title: Demetrius asks for continued loyalty and promises rewards
speaker: King Demetrius, by letter
note: The promised remissions and gifts are the reward named in the record’s title; extend to 10:27–28.

title: Alexander summons Jonathan to meet him at Ptolemais
speaker: King Alexander, by letter
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Reported written summons.

title: Alexander orders Jonathan stripped of his garments and clothed in purple
speaker: King Alexander
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Distinct honour preceding the protection order (ot-1-maccabees-v10-63); could instead extend that record.

title: Alexander appoints Jonathan general and district governor
speaker: King Alexander
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Enrolled among the First Friends and given military and civil office.

title: Apollonius challenges Jonathan to come down and fight in the plain
speaker: Apollonius
note: Challenge 'come down to us into the plain' (10:71); extend to 10:70–73 and retype Study Context as Command (cf. ot-2-kings-v14-8).

title: Alexander orders his cities to welcome Ptolemy as his father-in-law
speaker: King Alexander
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Reported order mentioned in passing; 11:1 is narrative.

title: Demetrius orders Jonathan to stop the siege and come to Ptolemais
speaker: King Demetrius II, by letter
note: Reported written order in the context verse, defied in 11:23.

title: Jonathan orders the siege of the citadel to continue
speaker: Jonathan
note: Reported order; he then takes elders and priests to the king at personal risk.

title: Jonathan asks Demetrius to remove the citadel garrison from Jerusalem
speaker: Jonathan
note: Reported request in the context verse, answered in 11:42–43.

title: Demetrius promises honours and asks Jonathan to send him troops
speaker: King Demetrius II
note: Royal request, met with three thousand men (11:44).

title: Antiochus VI confirms Jonathan as high priest and grants royal honours
speaker: the young King Antiochus, by letter
note: Confirms the high priesthood, appoints him over four districts, and grants purple and gold vessels.

title: Antiochus VI appoints Simon general from Tyre’s Ladder to Egypt
speaker: the young King Antiochus
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Separate appointment in the context verse; could be combined with the 11:57–58 record.

title: Jonathan sends envoys to renew friendship with Rome and Sparta
speaker: Jonathan
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Embassy and letters; the envoys’ charge is restated in the Spartan letter (12:16–17).

title: Jonathan’s letter asks Sparta to receive his envoys and reply
speaker: Jonathan the high priest, with the elders and priests, by letter
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: The letter of 12:6–18 has no record; its directives are the envoys’ charge (12:17) and the request for a reply (12:18).

title: Jonathan and the elders resolve to fortify Judea and isolate the citadel
speaker: Jonathan and the elders of the people
note: Council decision, like Asa’s fortification proposal (ot-2-chronicles-v14-6) and 1 Maccabees 4:36.

title: Tryphon orders his Friends and forces to obey Jonathan
speaker: Tryphon
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Deceptive honour leading to ot-1-maccabees-v12-45; could instead extend that record to 12:43–45.

title: The people acclaim Simon their leader and pledge to obey him
speaker: the people gathered in Jerusalem
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Acclamation with a pledge of obedience; compare ot-joshua-v1-18 and AUD-07-11-8.

title: The citadel garrison urges Tryphon to come through the wilderness with food
speaker: those in the citadel
note: Reported request carried by envoys; 13:20 is narrative.

title: Demetrius II confirms Judea’s strongholds and remits its offences and levies
speaker: King Demetrius II, by letter
recipient: Simon, the elders and the nation of the Jews
note: Royal decree answering Simon’s embassy (13:34); the letter is otherwise unrecorded.

title: Demetrius II opens royal enrollment to Jews and declares peace
speaker: King Demetrius II, by letter
note: Separate grant in the same letter; followed by the removal of the nations’ yoke (13:41).

title: Simon decrees a yearly celebration of the citadel’s capture
speaker: Simon
note: Annual festival for the 23rd of the second month (13:51); compare ot-1-maccabees-v4-59.

title: Simon appoints his son John commander of all the forces
speaker: Simon
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Appointment of John as commander, residing at Gazara.

title: Sparta resolves to honor the Jewish envoys and record their words
speaker: the rulers and people of Sparta, by letter
recipient: Simon the high priest and the Jews
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Foreign civic resolution quoted in a letter. 14:25 is a question leading to the recorded decree (14:41–49).

title: The assembly appoints Simon leader and high priest
speaker: the people, in the decree’s recital
note: Recital that the people made Simon leader and high priest, the same appointment as 14:41; 14:36 is narrative.

title: Antiochus VII confirms past remissions and lets Judea mint its own coins
speaker: King Antiochus VII, by letter
recipient: Simon and the nation of the Jews
note: Chapter 15 has no records; 15:5 was not flagged. The coinage grant is a distinct royal privilege.

title: Antiochus VII declares Jerusalem free and remits all royal debts forever
speaker: King Antiochus VII, by letter
recipient: Simon and the nation of the Jews
note: Freedom of Jerusalem, retention of weapons and strongholds, perpetual remission; later annulled (15:27).

title: Rome directs kings and countries not to make war on the Jews
speaker: Lucius, consul of the Romans
recipient: King Ptolemy and the kings and countries of 15:22–23
note: Roman circular decree protecting Judea and forbidding alliance with its enemies.

title: Rome orders fugitives from Judea handed over to Simon for judgment
speaker: Lucius, consul of the Romans
note: Extradition clause: offenders to be punished 'according to their law'.

title: Antiochus VII demands Simon surrender the cities or pay a thousand talents
speaker: King Antiochus VII, through Athenobius
note: Ultimatum after annulling earlier grants (15:27); Simon’s reply follows in 15:33–35.

title: Antiochus VII appoints Cendebaeus to rebuild Kedron and make war on Judea
speaker: King Antiochus VII
note: 15:41 records the order carried out 'as the king had ordered him'; 15:40 is narrative.

title: Nehemiah orders the remaining water poured over the larger stones
speaker: Nehemiah
note: Further ritual order in the fire episode; the prayer (1:24–29) is out of scope; AUD-16-1-20 covers only 1:20–21.

title: Jeremiah orders the deportees to take some of the altar fire
speaker: Jeremiah the prophet, as found in the records
note: Reported order distinct from AUD-16-2-2 (remember the law, 2:2–3); could instead extend that record to 2:1–3.

title: The Jerusalem letter invites Egypt’s Jews to send for the gathered books
speaker: the Jews of Jerusalem and Judea, by letter
note: Offer of Judas’s collected writings (cf. Nehemiah’s library, 2:13); the 2:16 request to observe the days is recorded.

title: Heliodorus advises the king to send only an enemy to Jerusalem
speaker: Heliodorus
note: Ironic counsel bearing witness that God guards the temple (3:39); advisers’ counsel is usually Instruction.

title: Menelaus urges Andronicus to murder Onias
speaker: Menelaus
topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
note: Reported incitement to murder; chapter 4 has no records.

title: Antiochus leaves Philip and Andronicus as overseers to afflict the people
speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
recipient: Philip in Jerusalem and Andronicus at Gerizim
note: Appointment of oppressive governors after the temple’s plunder (5:21).

title: Antiochus sends Apollonius to slaughter Jerusalem’s men and sell the rest
speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
note: Reported order of massacre and enslavement; parallel 1 Maccabees 1:29–32 is also unrecorded.

title: Apollonius orders his troops to parade under arms on the Sabbath
speaker: Apollonius
note: Reported order exploiting the Sabbath rest, followed by the massacre (5:26).

title: Eleazar refuses to mislead younger people by pretending to break the law
speaker: the narrator, of Eleazar
note: Opening of Eleazar’s martyrdom with the narrator’s 'as those ought to approach' maxim (6:20); 6:17 is a transition.

title: Antiochus orders the first brother mutilated and fried before his family
speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
note: Reported orders of torture after the refusal in 7:2; compare the massacre order AUD-16-5-11.

title: The brothers and their mother urge one another to die nobly
speaker: the brothers and their mother
note: Mutual exhortation citing Moses’ song (Deuteronomy 32:36); 7:2 states their shared resolve.

title: Better to die hoping in God’s promise of resurrection
speaker: the fourth brother
note: 'It is preferable…' saying; the judgment on the king is out of scope. 7:9 (P01145) is declaration only.

title: The mother urges her sons to hope in the Creator of life
speaker: the mother of the seven brothers
note: Her exhortation to each son; the later appeal to the youngest is ot-2-maccabees-v7-29.

title: Antiochus presses the youngest son and his mother to abandon the law
speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
recipient: the youngest brother and his mother
note: Inducement with oaths, wealth and office to abandon ancestral ways; then he urges the mother to persuade him.

title: A mother urges her youngest son to face death trusting God
speaker: the mother
note: Opening of the same appeal ('Son, have mercy on me…'); extend to 7:27–29.

title: Obey the law given through Moses, not the king’s ordinance
speaker: the youngest brother
note: Principle of obeying God’s law over a ruler; compare A051 (Acts 5:29). 7:31 is judgment.

title: The youngest son warns Antiochus not to exalt himself against Heaven’s children
speaker: the youngest brother
note: Warning like the sixth brother’s (ot-2-maccabees-v7-18); 7:35–36 announce judgment.

title: Ptolemy sends Nicanor and Gorgias to wipe out Judea’s people
speaker: Ptolemy, governor of Coele-Syria, at Philip’s request
recipient: Nicanor son of Patroclus and Gorgias
note: Parallel account of 1 Maccabees 3:38–39 (proposed under P01061); chapter 8 has no records.

title: Nicanor invites the coastal cities to buy Jewish captives
speaker: Nicanor
topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
note: Reported offer of ninety bodies for a talent to pay Rome’s tribute; compare 1 Maccabees 3:41.

title: Judas urges his men to fight nobly and trust the Almighty
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
note: Reported exhortation with the saying 'they trust in weapons… we trust in the Almighty God' (8:18).

title: Judas appoints his brothers over divisions and reads the sacred book
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Division commands, a public reading and the watchword 'God’s help' before battle.

title: Antiochus orders his charioteer to drive on to destroy Jerusalem
speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes
note: Reported order with an arrogant vow, answered by God’s plague (9:5); 9:2 is narrative.

title: Submit to God; no mortal should think himself equal to God
speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes, stricken
note: Maxim spoken in context verse 9:12; 9:11 narrates his coming to understanding.

title: Antiochus appoints his son Antiochus king as his successor
speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes, by letter
recipient: the Jews and his son Antiochus
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Designation of a successor, explained from his father’s practice; chapter 9 has no records.

title: Antiochus asks the Jews to stay loyal to him and his son
speaker: King Antiochus Epiphanes, by letter
note: Request in the dying king’s letter; its greetings (9:19–22, P01157) need no record.

title: Judas urges his men to share the danger and help their brothers
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
note: Reported battle exhortation; the prayer in 11:6 is out of scope.

title: Lysias proposes peace with the Jews on just terms
speaker: Lysias
note: Peace overture and Judas’s written requests granted by the king; compare ot-1-maccabees-v6-58.

title: Antiochus V tells Lysias to send the Jews pledges of peace
speaker: King Antiochus Eupator, by letter
note: Executive instruction following the decree of 11:25 (ot-2-maccabees-v11-25); 11:23 is its preamble.

title: Roman envoys tell the Jews to send word quickly on referred matters
speaker: Quintus Memmius and Titus Manius, Roman envoys
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Letter approving Lysias’s grants and asking for envoys; 11:38 is a farewell.

title: Joppa’s decree lures its Jews aboard boats and drowns them
speaker: the people of Joppa, by common decree
topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
note: Treacherous civic decree in the context verses; Judas’s orders in 12:5 lack content and 12:7 is narrative.

title: The defeated Arabs ask Judas for pledges of peace
speaker: the defeated Arab nomads
note: Reported request, granted with pledges (12:12).

title: The Jews urge Scythopolis to remain favorable to their people
speaker: Judas and his men
note: Reported thanks and request after the Scythopolitans’ humane treatment of local Jews.

title: Judas sends a sin offering to Jerusalem for the fallen
speaker: Judas Maccabeus, commended by the narrator
recipient: his men and the priests in Jerusalem
note: Adjacent gap, not flagged: collection, sin offering and the narrator’s teaching on prayer for the dead. 12:39 is narrative.

title: Antiochus V orders Menelaus executed at Beroea
speaker: King Antiochus Eupator
note: Reported execution order at Lysias’s prompting; 13:5–8 describe it as just retribution.

title: Judas and the elders resolve to march out before the king invades
speaker: Judas Maccabeus with the elders
note: Council decision after the three days of prayer recorded in AUD-16-13-10.

title: Judas urges his men to die fighting for law and temple
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
note: Reported exhortation to fight for laws, temple, city, homeland and civic life.

summary: All 169 passages reviewed: 127 findings (108 new, 14 extend, 5 parallel), chiefly unrecorded royal letters, appointments and battle orders in 1–2 Maccabees and covenants, reforms and prophetic directions in 2 Chronicles; prayers, blessings and narrative candidates need nothing.
